subsystems.name: Host material
subsystems.role: supports the anyonic excitations that carry quantum information.
parts: two-dimensional electron gas in a semiconductor heterostructure

subsystems.name: Anyon control
subsystems.role: creates, moves and braids anyons to encode and manipulate information.

subsystems.name: Readout
subsystems.role: measures the fusion outcome of anyons without destroying the encoded state.

subsystems.name: Cryogenic environment
subsystems.role: keeps the system cold and clean enough for topological order to survive.

subsystems.name: Classical control and decoding
subsystems.role: interprets measurements and manages error correction or logical operations.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the host material
buildSteps.detail: Grow a high-mobility semiconductor heterostructure or a semiconductor–superconductor nanowire network, then pattern it into a device with nanoscale gates and electrodes.

buildSteps.title: Cool the device
buildSteps.detail: Mount it in a dilution refrigerator and cool to a few thousandths of a kelvin, where anyonic excitations can exist without thermal disruption.

buildSteps.title: Create anyons
buildSteps.detail: Tune magnetic fields and gate voltages to drive the system into a topological phase, nucleating anyons at chosen locations.

buildSteps.title: Initialise the memory
buildSteps.detail: Arrange anyons in a specific configuration so that their fusion space encodes a known logical state.

buildSteps.title: Store and protect
buildSteps.detail: Leave the anyons unbraided; local perturbations cannot change the global topological state, so the information persists.

buildSteps.title: Perform logical operations
buildSteps.detail: Move anyons around one another (braid) to apply unitary transformations to the stored information.

buildSteps.title: Read out
buildSteps.detail: Bring anyons together to fuse them and measure the resulting charge, revealing the logical state.

buildSteps.title: Scale up
buildSteps.detail: Fabricate arrays of many anyons or integrate with surface-code error correction to build a large, reliable memory.

prerequisites.why: fractional quantum Hall states and Majorana modes are candidates, but conclusive evidence is still lacking.
modern semiconductor fabs and dilution refrigerators can build and cool the required devices.
topological codes like the surface code show how to protect logical qubits from local errors.
no experiment has convincingly demonstrated controlled braiding of non-Abelian anyons.
wiring and multiplexing thousands of signals at millikelvin temperatures remains a challenge.

pathway.milestone: small surface-code logical qubits on conventional hardware and contested signatures of Majorana modes
pathway.unlocks: proof that topological protection can be engineered in practice.

pathway.milestone: conclusive demonstration of non-Abelian anyons and their braiding in a solid-state device
pathway.unlocks: a physical platform for topological quantum memory.

pathway.milestone: a logical qubit whose lifetime far exceeds that of its physical components
scalable arrays of topological qubits with built-in error correction
pathway.unlocks: fault-tolerant quantum computing and long-term quantum memory.
